description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, b2-11).  Probe vs perl 5.40.3: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/endstatus1.pl (run WITHOUT a pipe so the shell's rc is the program's).  The idiom: cleanup code that must not clobber the status (`END { my $rc = $?; cleanup(); $? = $rc }`) and test harness wrappers that force a status.  perl: `exit N` sets `$?` = N before END blocks run; after the last END block the process exits with whatever `$?` holds; a `die` at top level makes it the die's status (errno or 255).  WHERE: the runtime's exit path (p-exit / the END runner).  Low priority; runtime-only; bar = full sweep + companion op/die_exit.t run/exit.t legs + a guard row using `system($^X ...)`-free shape (the Pl/t helpers can read a child's rc).


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) -- closes #2009, #2031 and #1426 together (one seam) ===
ROOT: `$?` was a raw `(defvar $? 0)`, not a box, and every perl-side write goes through box-set, which is a no-op on a non-box -- so `$? = N`, `$? += 1`, `$? |= 8`, `($?) = (4)`, `$$ref = 2` through \$?, and every assignment inside END were lost; and the exit hook never gave END the pending status.
FIX (runtime only, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp):
  * `$?` is a MAGIC box (the $. / $! shape): getter/setter over *p-status*; the setter stores perl's INTEGER (`$? = "7abc"` -> 7, `3.7` -> 3, probed).  Every runtime writer (system, qx, wait/waitpid, close on a pipe incl. the #2006(a) save/restore, exit, the END phase) goes through ONE %p-set-status that writes whatever $? is BOUND to -- so inside `local $?` the child's status lands in the local box and the outer value returns at scope exit (probed: in=3 sys=256 out=14, as perl).  Readers use %p-status.
  * THE END PHASE is a named function %p-run-end-phase (was an anonymous lambda): exit and the uncaught-die hook record the leaving status in *p-exit-status* via ONE %p-exit-process; the phase sets $? to it (0 at the natural end, even after a failed system), runs the ENDs LIFO (each sees the previous one's $?; exit inside one ends that block, #738), flushes, and exits with $? & 255 only when it changed (a nested sb-ext:exit is the LAST thing, as before).  *p-end-exit-code* is gone -- its job is $? now.
PROBES (scratch/s495f/p-end.sh, 14 programs, stdout + rc vs perl 5.40.3; p-status.pl 12 spellings): identical except `local $?;` with NO initialiser, which reads undef where perl's magic reads 0 (the v1-seam local emission gives `(make-p-box nil)`; residue, not filed separately -- rare, reading $? right after a bare `local $?`).  `pcl -e` and a cached `pcl FILE` run give the same status (e=3 rc=5 / rc=4 twice).  POSIX::_exit still skips END.
GUARDS: Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t -- rows 11 and 13 were INVERSE guards naming #1427/#1426 ("closing it FAILS here"); they failed as designed and now assert perl's answer (a method call on undef is a p-die since #2051's member, exit 255; `$? = 256; die` exits 1); plus 10 new rows (END phase + $? spellings, stdout AND rc vs perl), 8 of them failing on the 3d9b3712 extraction (the 2 that pass there are the inverse guards: exit-in-END and POSIX::_exit).  everyday programs/env-exit-end -> same (row edited out).
subject: EDGE (pre-existing): inside an END block `$?` is 0 instead of the pending exit status, and assigning `$?` in END does not change the process's exit code -- `END { $? = 5 } exit 3` exits 5 in perl, 3 in PCL; `END { print $? } exit 3` prints 3 in perl, 0 in PCL
